e-13199.knowledge_point: Listing the Elements in a Power Set
e-13199.worked_solution:
The power set of $A,$ denoted $\mathcal{P}(A),$ is the set that contains every possible subset of $A,$ including the empty set $\emptyset.$

So, let's list all possible subsets of $A$ using a tree diagram.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14098182/assets/b3af256806e0aeb0396564320800f908c66d5830ab46e676dfc51ceab24154f6.png)

According to our diagram, the subsets of $A$ are

$$
\emptyset = \{\},\quad \{2\},\quad \{4\},\quad \{ \{8\} \}, \quad \{2, 4\},\quad \{2, \{8\}\},\quad \{4, \{8\}\},\quad\{2, 4, \{8\}\}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\mathcal{P}(A) = \{\emptyset, \{2\}, \{4\}, \{\{8\}\}, \{2, 4\}, \{2, \{8\}\}, \{4, \{8\}\},\{2, 4, \{8\}\}\}.
$$

e-13200.knowledge_point: Computing the Cardinality of a Power Set
e-13200.worked_solution:
For any set $Y,$ we have $\left|\mathcal{P}(Y)\right| = 2^{\left| Y \right|}.$

In this case, $\left| Y \right| = 4,$ so we have

$$
\left| \mathcal{P}(Y) \right| = 2^{\left| Y \right|} = 2^{4} = 16.
$$

Remember that $\{ 3,5 \}$ is a single element in the set $Y.$

after.worked_solution:
The power set of $X,$ denoted $P(X),$ is the set that contains every possible subset of $X,$ including the empty set $∅.$

So, let's list all possible subsets of $X$ using a tree diagram. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14098182/assets/580d7c32378a2af641fb1066cec4ec24cc6c5b140ccf9475f9a3e3a68367d30d.png)

According to our diagram, the subsets of $X$ are

$$
∅={},\,{2},\,{4},\,{8},\,{2,4},\,{2,8},\,{4,8},\,{2,4,8}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
P(X)={∅,{2},{4},{8},{2,4},{2,8},{4,8},{2,4,8}}.
$$

after.worked_solution:
The power set of $T,$ denoted $P(T),$ is the set that contains every possible subset of $T,$ including the empty set $∅.$

So, let's list all possible subsets of $T$ using a tree diagram.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14098182/assets/916d0207e217da90b6421244f0f02d59d8f9dbafc2a7045033eab5ae2b69740e.png)

According to our diagram, the subsets of $T$ are

$$
∅={},\,{r},\,{s},\,{t},\,{r,s},\,{r,t},\,{s,t},\,{r,s,t}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
P(T)={∅,{r},{s},{t},{r,s},{r,t},{s,t},{r,s,t}}.
$$
